title: TensorCore Softmax Fusion for Paged-KV Prototype
body:
Goal:
- Prototype a kernel variant that leverages Tensor Cores to fuse the softmax (scale+exp+sum+div) and the downstream matmul/weighted-accumulate in FlashAttention-like flows, optimized for paged KV scenarios where KV pages may fault in/out.

Motivation / What problem we hit:
- For long-context chat workloads (SEQ>8k), paged KV introduces irregular memory accesses and stalls when pages are missing.
- Classic FlashAttention saves memory bandwidth by streaming attention but has separate softmax and GEMM phases; memory ops and synchronizations are a significant part of per-token latency.
- Tensor Cores (TF32/FP16/FP8) can accelerate compute-heavy softmax+mul chains if we can expose fused math to wmma/cublasLt-like ops and reduce shared memory traffic.

Constraints and assumptions:
- Target hardware: A100/A800/Blackwell (support for wmma mma.sync or equivalent).
- We must preserve numerical stability for FP16/TF32, and provide a deterministic FP32 fallback for customers that require bit-identical outputs.
- Paged KV model: KV pages are 1MB-ish shards (configurable); page fetch latency (network+IO) is non-negligible ~0.5-5ms.
- Kernel should not block on page faults: use staged execution with continuation/resume semantics.

High-level design idea:
1) Split attention tile into stages: load-query-block, compute-QK partials, fused softmax+scale using TensorCores, apply to V (fused matmul-accumulate).
2) Represent softmax operation as a small GEMM-like pipeline where exponentiation and reduction are implemented via numerically-stable tile-level reductions, using TF32/FP16 with a compensated FP32 accumulator when needed.
3) Use a tiny custom microkernel (wmma-backed) that accepts precomputed max and sum per tile to perform exp(x - max)/sum in a group and immediately multiply the result into V fragments — avoiding writing normalized weights back to global memory.
4) For paged KV, introduce a page-presence hint bitmask passed into kernel launch; kernel does fast-path for fully-present tiles, and a continuation path for tiles with missing pages (enqueue work to prefetch and mark continuation token).

Kernel sketch / stages (informal):
- Stage A: Tiling and Q-loading. load Q tile to registers / fragment.
- Stage B: Compute Q*K^T partials for K-fragments that are present. For K fragments that map to missing pages, write placeholder zeros and atomically append tile-id to PF queue.
- Stage C (fusion): For each QK partial group: compute tile-wise max via warp reduction, compute exp-mapped fragment using wmma tensor ops, compute sum via warp-level reduction, normalize in-place in registers, immediately wmma-gemm-mul with V-fragments accumulating to output fragment.
- Stage D: Write output accumulations to global output.

Key micro-optimizations to try:
- Use half-precision inputs and TF32 accumulators for the softmax exp/sum path. Consider FP8 for V in inference-heavy models but evaluate quality.
- Keep normalized attention weights in registers only. Use shuffle shuffles and warp reductions to avoid shared memory whenever tile fits warp fragments.
- For larger tiles (multi-warp), use small shared memory staging but keep lifetime minimal.
- Use asynchronous copy (cp.async) for K/V page fragments when page present to hide access latency relative to compute.
- Provide a per-launch parameter "prefetch_threshold_ms" that decides whether kernel will attempt to prefetch missing pages or bail to continuation.

Paged-KV interaction model (pragmatic):
- Kernel receives a presence bitmap: for each KV-page-id referenced in the launch, bit=1 if present, 0 if missing.
- Missing page detection logic: kernel marks tile as incomplete, writes tile key into a small per-SM buffer (ring) which the runtime polls and triggers async prefetch.
- Runtime-Driver contract: continuation tokens contain program counter / tile offsets; a resumed kernel will skip already-computed tiles.
- Useful optimization: for pages that are slow to return, upstream routing can map requests to a model variant with smaller KV (e.g., chunked attention) and the runtime can fall back automatically.

Experimental plan and metrics:
- Microbench targets: 99th p50/p90 token latency for sequences 2k, 8k, 16k under mixed page-fault rates {0%, 5%, 20%}.
- Throughput: tokens/sec for batch sizes [1,4,16,64] comparing baseline FlashAttention kernel vs fused-TensorCore prototype.
- Accuracy: compare generation deltas and logit differences vs FP32 reference for a small eval set.
- Resource counters: SM utilization, tensor-core utilization, L2 bandwidth, global load/store rates, page-fault counts, and PCIe/NVLink bandwidth impact for prefetches.

Bench harness notes:
- Use existing microbench infra: tools/bench/attn-microbench and extend runner to toggle presence bitmaps.
- Add synthetic KV page delay injector (configurable delay distribution) to emulate network or disk-backed KV.
- Collect traces with nvprof/nsys and include per-kernel timeline to verify overlap between cp.async prefetch and tensor-core compute.

Open questions / risks (brainstorm):
- Numerical stability: fused exp/sum in reduced precision may bias head distributions for long context. Need compensated reductions; maybe keep the reduction in FP32.
- Complexity of continuation semantics: if many tiles miss, kernel overhead of marking and bailing may dominate. Might need a fast exit early if missing fraction > X%.
- Warp-level vs block-level design tradeoff for sequences > 32k.
- Portability across GPU generations: not all have same wmma semantics; need fallbacks and autotuning.

Implementation TODOs (short):
- [ ] Design small tensorcore microkernel for fused softmax+mul (owner: Arjun)
- [ ] Add presence-bitmap ABI to kernel launcher / runtime (owner: Maya)
- [ ] Hook up PF queue in runtime (owner: Sofia)
- [ ] Add continuation token mechanism and resume path (owner: Noah)
- [ ] Bench harness instrumentation and synthetic delay (owner: Maya + infra)

Notes to self / rough thoughts:
- If we succeed in keeping weights in-register until multiply-with-V, expect a 10-30% latency drop for fully-present cases due to reduced global writes. For partial page case, benefit depends on fraction of present tiles.
- Might get extra wins by combining with precached average-key statistics: if we detect very peaked attention (max >> others), we can skip full exp for small tail via approximate cutoff.

References / links:
- See prior flash-attn drafts in this dir for scheduling ideas (but this code path tries to use tensor-cores rather than classic shared-memory heavy tiling).
- Related PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-runtime/pull/842 (proto kernel harness)

Next sync / milestone:
- Plan quick spike: implement microkernel and bench baseline by 2025-11-26. Demo results in weekly runtime sync.

Unresolved: vendor-driver interactions for prefetch triggers; need SRE/infra input on safe async IO scheduling.
